materials.name: Inconel 718
materials.note: Inconel 718 is a precipitation-hardened Ni-Cr-Fe superalloy used as high-strength, corrosion-resistant billet and forging stock from cryogenic service to elevated-temperature aerospace, energy, and harsh-environment applications.

materials.name: Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al
materials.note: Ti-10V-2Fe-3Al (Ti-10-2-3, TB6, UNS R56410) is a near-beta titanium alloy for deep-hardenable aerospace forgings with strong strength-toughness balance and hot-die forgeability; Beta-C is a different alloy and must not be cross-mapped.

materials.name: Ti-6Al-4V
materials.note: Ti-6Al-4V is the workhorse α+β titanium alloy used widely as billet, bar, and forging stock, combining high specific strength, corrosion resistance, weldability, and heat-treat response.

materials.name: Ti80
materials.note: Ti80 is a Chinese near-alpha titanium alloy, standardized as TA31 in GB/T 3620.1 and used for marine / seawater structural service; nominal composition Ti-6Al-3Nb-2Zr-1Mo.

materials.name: Waspaloy
materials.note: Waspaloy is a wrought, age-hardenable Ni-base superalloy billet material used for high-strength gas-turbine rotating hardware and other oxidation-resistant elevated-temperature components.

materials.name: A-286
materials.note: A-286 (Alloy 660) is a precipitation-hardenable Fe-Ni-Cr austenitic high-strength alloy used for fasteners and hot-section hardware up to about 704°C.

materials.name: Inconel 706
materials.note: Inconel 706 (UNS N09706) is a precipitation-hardenable Ni-Fe-Cr superalloy designed for high-strength, comparatively workable large-section aerospace and gas-turbine forgings with two canonical heat-treatment tracks for creep-focused and tensile-focused applications.

materials.name: Haynes 282
materials.note: Haynes 282 is a wrought gamma-prime-strengthened Ni-base superalloy (UNS N07208) developed for high-temperature structural service in aero and industrial gas-turbine applications where creep strength, thermal stability, weldability, and fabricability are all required.

materials.name: Alloy 263
materials.note: Alloy 263 is a wrought precipitation-hardenable Ni-Co-Cr-Mo superalloy (UNS N07263 / W.Nr. 2.4650) used in high-temperature aerospace and gas-turbine service under trade names such as HAYNES 263, NIMONIC alloy 263, ATI C-263, and PER263.

materials.name: Inconel 625
materials.note: Inconel 625 is a wrought Ni-Cr-Mo-Nb alloy (UNS N06625 / EN 2.4856) whose baseline strength comes primarily from solid-solution strengthening rather than precipitation hardening; it is widely procured across ASTM, AMS, BS, DIN, ISO, and JIS product-form standards.

materials.name: Nimonic 90
materials.note: Nimonic 90 is a wrought Ni-Cr-Co age-hardenable superalloy strengthened by Ti and Al additions, used for turbine blades, disks, forgings, ring sections, and other high-temperature gas-turbine hardware to about 920°C.

materials.name: GH4698
materials.note: GH4698 is a Chinese wrought precipitation-hardened Ni-based superalloy used for heavily loaded turbine and compressor disks plus other rotating gas-turbine components, with commonly cited long-term service around 750-800°C.

materials.name: GH4720Li
materials.note: GH4720Li is a Chinese wrought low-interstitial Ni-Cr-Co gamma-prime-strengthened superalloy for turbine disks and other rotating hot-section hardware below about 750°C; accessible sources repeatedly relate it to the Udimet 720Li / 720 alloy family, but foreign equivalence claims are not uniformly backed by primary standards text.

materials.name: FGH96
materials.note: FGH96 is a Chinese powder-metallurgy Ni-based gamma-prime-strengthened superalloy for turbine disks and other rotating hot-section components; open literature repeatedly treats it as a second-generation disk alloy with chemistry near the Rene 88DT family.

materials.name: Alloy 901
materials.note: Alloy 901 is a wrought age-hardenable Ni-Fe-Cr superalloy with Mo, Ti, and Al additions, used for gas-turbine engine disks, shafts, rings, casings, and seals to about 600°C.

materials.name: Incoloy 903
materials.note: Incoloy 903 is a wrought low-expansion Ni-Fe-Co age-hardenable superalloy with high strength, nearly constant modulus, and low thermal expansion for rocket-engine hardware, steam-turbine bolts, springs, and related precision high-temperature components.

materials.name: Incoloy 907
materials.note: Incoloy 907 is a wrought low-expansion Ni-Fe-Co age-hardenable superalloy for gas-turbine seals, shafts, casings, and other structural parts where high strength and low thermal expansion are needed.

materials.name: Incoloy 909
materials.note: Incoloy 909 is a wrought low-expansion Ni-Fe-Co age-hardenable superalloy for gas-turbine vanes, casings, shafts, shrouds, and rocket-engine hardware where high strength and low thermal expansion are required.

materials.name: Incoloy 925
materials.note: Incoloy 925 is a wrought age-hardenable Ni-Fe-Cr alloy with Mo, Cu, Ti, and Al additions, used for oil-and-gas tubulars, valves, hangers, packers, marine shafting, and high-strength corrosion-resistant hardware.

materials.name: Inconel 600
materials.note: Inconel 600 is a wrought nickel-chromium-iron solid-solution alloy used for high-temperature oxidation and corrosion-resistant service in heat-treating, chemical processing, and thermal equipment.

materials.name: Inconel 690
materials.note: Inconel 690 is a wrought high-chromium nickel alloy designed for excellent resistance to oxidizing and chloride-bearing aqueous environments, including nuclear steam-generator service.

materials.name: Haynes 188
materials.note: Haynes 188 is a wrought cobalt-nickel-chromium-tungsten alloy used for combustors and other gas-turbine hot-section components that require strong oxidation and hot-corrosion resistance.

materials.name: Haynes 230
materials.note: Haynes 230 is a wrought nickel-chromium-tungsten-molybdenum superalloy known for strong oxidation resistance, thermal stability, and high-temperature strength in aerospace and industrial-heating service.

materials.name: Hastelloy X
materials.note: Hastelloy X is a wrought nickel-chromium-iron-molybdenum alloy used for combustor, furnace, and chemical-process components that require oxidation resistance and high-temperature strength.

materials.name: GH710
materials.note: GH710 is a Chinese nickel-base precipitation-strengthened superalloy that secondary cross-reference sources associate with the GH4710 / Udimet 710 family for hot-section aerospace applications.

materials.name: GH4780
materials.note: GH4780 is a wrought Chinese nickel-base superalloy studied for microstructural evolution and heat-treatment response in disk and hot-section applications.

materials.name: FGH4097
materials.note: FGH4097 is a powder-metallurgy nickel-base disk superalloy reported in open fatigue-crack-growth literature as a newer PM alloy alongside FGH4096 and N18.

materials.name: K4169
materials.note: K4169 is a cast nickel-base superalloy in the Alloy 718 / GH4169 family used for hot-section castings, with currently accessible evidence coming mainly from secondary datasheet and corrosion-study sources.

materials.name: K418B
materials.note: K418B is a cast nickel-base superalloy that secondary sources commonly compare to the IN713C / Alloy 713 family for turbine blade and vane applications.

materials.name: K417G
materials.note: K417G is a cast nickel-base superalloy that secondary and literature sources relate to the Rene 100 / IN731 class of precipitation-strengthened turbine-blade alloys.

materials.name: K648
materials.note: K648 is a cast nickel-base superalloy used for high-temperature casting applications and currently represented here from secondary supplier composition summaries and process notes.

materials.name: GH4099
materials.note: GH4099 is a wrought Chinese nickel-base precipitation-strengthened superalloy represented here from secondary datasheet and literature sources with partial open evidence only.

materials.name: A-100
materials.note: A-100 is interpreted here as the Aermet 100 ultrahigh-strength alloy-steel family based on the accessible aerospace materials references; this mapping is seeded with an explicit caveat and should be revisited if a different A-100 designation is intended.
